spec_issues: The deciding rule, 'It may not skip unlikely next tokens', appears only in the public overview. The prompt the agents received says only: keep the public API, assistant-token masking and normalisation unchanged, and meet the tolerances in bench/utils/benchmark_config.json. Agents could infer the rule only from the starter comment 'Set filter_eps=None to avoid any token filtering', the oracle docstring ('Omitting small softmax contributions distorts many small rows at once') and the task id ('...-without-changing-its-gradients').

The rule does not say where 'skipping' ends and low-precision rounding begins. The overview explicitly allows extra error up to a fixed margin, and every high-scoring compliant solution quantises the softmax tail to 4-8 bits, which zeroes the smallest entries. Fable rwkZkp2 uses e4m3 with a per-token scale capped at tau=3e-3, so entries below about 1e-8 round to 0. Fable XLG9UMd and Argon tAA7K6K use NVFP4 with 16-entry blocks, so entries below about 1/24 of their block's maximum round to 0. None of the three adds a correction for what it zeroes. The rule as enforced separates explicit selection and omission from uniform quantisation, but this boundary is not written anywhere.

The disqualification process is undisclosed. Tolerance-valid runs (valid=1, 3.46-3.79x) were zeroed with only the reason 'Forbidden computational shortcut'. Argon tAA7K6K is valid=0 with no reason given.
verifier_issues: The automated tolerance does not enforce the no-skipping rule. The row_outlier_frac check was written to catch omitted softmax entries, yet all 5 disqualified trials passed it (valid=1 with an objective). Enforcement therefore rests entirely on the undisclosed review.

The public harness is robust against the usual kernel exploits. Weights are re-noised every call (batch_weight with a per-call seed), so cross-call caching is useless. Baseline and candidate calls are interleaved in separate SIGSTOPped workers. A gradient fingerprint is taken after the reply, so deferred work is detected. The FP32 oracle runs outside the timer. No patch edits bench/ (XLG9UMd only adds a new file, bench/dev_check.py). No trial caches results across calls or defers work.

Specialisation is to the fixed Qwen3 head and to the GPU, not to the evaluation data: Argon tAA7K6K hard-codes lm_weight.shape == (151936, 2048) and sm_120a; GPT-6 VPUizq6 requires compute capability (12,0) and CUDA 13; Kimi 98hzSX3 requires d % 2048 == 0; Grok ojLuB26 uses tile-top buffers 'only worth it on the benchmark shape'. All of them fall back to a general path. Kimi ptvCExN uses a fixed exp reference of 40 ('Logits on the benchmark data stay within [-40, 46]') with a +80 clamp and no fallback, which is fragile outside this data but gains it essentially no speed.

Argon tAA7K6K loads a prebuilt _fast_qwen3_ce_ext.so that the text patch cannot carry, falling back to compiling with load_inline. Its tolerance margin was thin (one local run failed d_hidden row_outlier_frac 6.3e-4 > 5e-4 at step [1394]). Either could explain its valid=0.
task_level.noise: baseline_objective varies from 103,475 to 107,608 tok/s across the 12 trials, a 4% range (about 1.2% coefficient of variation). Reward is a ratio of candidate to baseline measured in the same paired, interleaved run, so most of that drift cancels. Repeated local runs of one artifact varied by about 1-3% (Argon tAA7K6K: 4.26-4.39x). The gaps between compliant models are far larger: Fable 3.70x/2.49x, Kimi 1.97x/1.94x, Flash 1.74x/1.66x, so noise does not affect the scored ranking. Among the disqualified runs, however, GPT-6 C67AxpK (3.697x) and Fable XLG9UMd (3.701x) differ by 0.1%, which is pure noise. Grok ojLuB26 (3.79x) would top the task if the disqualifications were reversed.
task_level.epoch_rationale: Under the published no-skipping rule the final scores look right: all 5 disqualified trials explicitly omit tail entries and no scored trial does, and Fable wins among compliant runs by a wide margin. But the rule was not in the agent prompt, the automated verifier does not enforce it, and it is applied by an undisclosed process. If the rule does not bind agents, Grok ojLuB26 (3.79x) wins instead, so the winner turns on a policy question the public data cannot settle.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Every score comes from known kernel techniques: computing the logits once instead of recomputing them, fusing the softmax, and low-precision GEMMs (int8 with SmoothQuant-style scaling, MXFP8, NVFP4) with the dominant entries recomputed exactly, as in LLM.int8()-style outlier handling. The highest raw speedups (GPT-6, Grok, Argon z3Viy4a) came from approximating d_hidden by dropping tail entries (top-16 union, p<1e-6 cutoff, or relative cutoff plus a global 'tail centre'), which the overview forbids. Fable's top scores sit close to the same line: it explicitly rejected filtering (XLG9UMd step [33]) but accepted that 4-bit rounding zeroes tiny entries (step [60]). Nothing here is new research; the compliant gains are solid engineering.

trials.approach: A single fused Triton pass computes the logits once with an int8 GEMM, using SmoothQuant-style channel smoothing. It stores E=exp(logit - target logit) in bf16 and recomputes the ~3-5 dominant entries per token exactly in fp32. The backward runs one MXFP8 GEMM for d_weight and one NVFP4 GEMM for d_hidden over all V entries; entries above tau are taken out of the quantised operand and added back exactly. Speedup 3.70x.
evidence: patch linear_ce_kernels.py docstring: forward is 'one int8 GEMM for the logits'; the dominant entries 'are recomputed exactly afterwards (_int8_fix_kernel)'; d_hidden is 'NVFP4 ... A_4 = fp4(E / Z_est) with the selected entries S_n zeroed', and the selected entries are 'recomputed exactly in fp32'. Every vocabulary column enters the GEMM.

_emit_fp4_dh_from_p: xq = tl.where(sel | is_tgt, 0.0, p * prescale), then per-16-entry e4m3 block scales. Non-selected entries are quantised, not removed. e2m1 rounding still zeroes entries below about 1/24 of their block's maximum, with no correction.
step [33]: 'I'm deciding against filtering'. step [60]: 'flushing tiny entries seems tolerable here'. The agent knowingly kept the computation dense and accepted quantisation underflow.
_use_fast_path is generic (dtype, D % 32 == 0, int32 addressing) with no shape or GPU pinning. No bench/ file is edited; bench/dev_check.py is a new helper.

trials.approach: A fused Triton forward stores the max-shifted logits in fp16. A split kernel keeps entries with p >= 3e-3, plus the target, exactly as sparse fp32 triples. The rest of the tail goes to e4m3 with a per-token scale for d_hidden and to e5m2 with a global scale for d_weight, followed by two torch._scaled_mm FP8 GEMMs and exact sparse fix-ups. Speedup 2.49x.
evidence: patch fused_linear_ce_triton.py, _lce_bwd_fp8_split_kernel: small = tl.where(large | ..., 0.0, p) is written in full to Buf1 (e4m3) and Buf2 (e5m2); 'large' entries go to exact triples. Tail entries are quantised rather than skipped.

The per-token e4m3 scale is bounded by min(1-p_target, tau)+1e-5 (bound line ~356), so entries below about 1e-8 round to zero in d_hidden. That is about 100x below Grok a4oLpi5's explicit 1e-6 cutoff, and it is a precision floor rather than a selection step.

The fallback to the 16-bit path for unsupported devices, slot overflow or very peaked softmax is generic; the path is not shape-pinned. The exception AgentContinuationStalledError did not affect the scored artifact.

trials.approach: Chunked (8192 tokens) torch.mm with fp32 logits, then a Triton row kernel computes the LSE and writes bf16 softmax-minus-one-hot. Two cuBLAS GEMMs give d_hidden and d_weight, all inside forward, and backward returns the stored gradients. The speedup over the starter's double recompute (1.74x) comes from computing the logits once.
evidence: patch fast_linear_ce.py: logits = torch.mm(h_chunk, weight_t, out_dtype=torch.float32), then fast_cross_entropy_kernel stores the gradient for every column (grad.to(tl.bfloat16)). Dense, nothing is skipped.
The dispatch only checks dtype, CUDA and softcap; no shape specialisation.

trials.approach: Same design as 267yivH: chunked fp32 cuBLAS logits, then a fused Triton online-softmax kernel writes bf16 probabilities minus one-hot, then two cuBLAS GEMMs. Speedup 1.66x.
evidence: patch fast_linear_ce.py: _fast_softmax_xent_kernel 'Pass 2: compute softmax probabilities - one_hot(target) and store in bfloat16' over all V; torch.mm(probs, lm_weight) and d_weight.addmm_(probs.T, h_chunk).
No thresholding or sparsity anywhere in the 295-line patch.

trials.approach: A custom CUDA/cuBLASLt extension hard-coded for V=151936, D=2048 and sm_120a. It runs an FP8 forward with outlier hidden channels handled separately, keeps the top-4 entries plus the target exactly, and builds NVFP4 operands for both backward GEMMs. Locally valid at 4.39x, but officially valid=0 with no reason given.
evidence: Locally valid: step [1438] public run {"valid": 1, ..., "speedup": 4.388891016908835}.

Thin tolerance margin: step [1394] 'INVALID ... d_hidden row_outlier_frac 6.343e-04 > 5.0e-04' and 'row_decile_rel_l2 4.011e-01 > 3.0e-01' on the shape-4 batches. A failure on the 35 held-out sequences is plausible.

_fast_qwen3_ce.py loads a prebuilt '_fast_qwen3_ce_ext.so' if one exists, otherwise compiles with load_inline. The .so the agent built and copied into the package cannot be carried by a text patch, so the private run had to compile (or fail).

No explicit tail omission: ce_pass2_all3fp8_kernel quantises every entry to NVFP4, zeroing only the exactly handled v1..v5 entries; whole blocks become zero only when their e4m3 scale underflows. This is the same family as Fable XLG9UMd, not z3Viy4a.
Shape pinning: dispatch requires lm_weight.shape == (151936, 2048), which is the fixed Qwen3 head, so it is not data specialisation.
Missing: the private verifier log or the disqualification reason.

trials.approach: Triton/cuBLASLt FP8/FP4 pipeline that marks confident 'only_y' rows as having no sparse entries and zeroes the tail block scales of 'dead' token tiles, using hand-tuned lse thresholds. Tail contributions are explicitly dropped for selected tokens.
evidence: patch linear_ce.py, _lse_and_sparse_only_kernel: only_y = (m == x_y) & (d * (1.0 - tau) < 1.0), then tl.store(cnt_ptr, 0) for those rows.

_zero_dead_tail_scales_kernel writes zero scales (tl.zeros((64, 2), dtype=tl.uint8)) for 'dead' tiles, selected by lse < dead_lse_th with magic constants 29.0 / 32.5 / 33.20. This removes tail entries rather than quantising them.

trials.approach: A single FP16-anchored projection. d_hidden is a sparse sum over entries above a per-row cutoff, and d_weight comes from a reduced-rank (rank 127) projection with sparse residual corrections, so sub-cutoff entries are not individually computed for either gradient. 3.70x, tolerance-valid.
evidence: patch dense_linear_ce.py backward: sparse_hidden_grad[(n, ...)](weight, indices, values, counts, ...) with cutoffs from 'tl.store(Cutoff + row, EPS * tl.exp(other_lse - lse))'.
d_weight = lowrank_weight_gradient(derivatives, states, ...) where linear_ce_lowrank.py is 'Reduced-rank classifier gradients with sparse residual corrections' (rank=127, eps=.015).
summary.json: valid=1, speedup 3.697. The tolerance passed, so the disqualification came from code review.

trials.approach: Centred MXFP8 projection. d_weight uses the full MXFP8 product over all classes, but d_hidden keeps only entries above theta=0.003 times the row maximum (cap 4096). Each token's remaining tail is replaced by its tail mass times one global class-mass-weighted mean weight row (the 'tail centre'). Gated to compute capability (12,0) with CUDA 13. 3.52x.
evidence: patch linear_ce_refined.py _compute: kernels._cut(... theta, cap), then _select / _refine build the sparse d_hidden; then 'center = pm.sum(0); kernels._add_center[...](dh, mass, center, n, d, 1024)'. Tail entries are not computed per token.
linear_ce_sparse.py docstring: 'Hidden gradients use sparse large terms and a probability-mass-preserving tail correction'; _RELATIVE_CUTOFF = 0.001.

linear_ce.py dispatch: use_blackwell requires torch.cuda.get_device_capability(...) == (12, 0) and torch.version.cuda.startswith('13.'), so it is GPU-specialised (falls back to the chunked path elsewhere).

trials.approach: A single logits pass with MX/FP4 quantisation for d_weight. d_hidden is a sparse gather over entries with p >= 1e-6 (up to 8192 per row), and the rest of the softmax tail is dropped. 3.46x.
evidence: patch fast_linear_ce.py: '# Softmax tail below this probability is dropped from d_hidden.' _SPARSE_EPS = 1e-6, _SPARSE_KMAX = 8192.
'# Sparse d_hidden drops a softmax tail that does not move the tolerance' (use_sparse = ctx.needs_input_grad[0] and n_tokens >= 256 ...).
step [13]: the agent had itself rejected 'vocab splitting with early exit' as approximate, then shipped a sparse tail drop anyway.

trials.approach: Custom CUDA top-16 per row. The d_hidden GEMM runs only over the union of the per-row top-16 columns plus labels; all other columns are omitted. Tile-top buffers are enabled only for the benchmark shape. 3.79x, the highest raw speedup.
evidence: patch fast_linear_ce.py: '# Columns kept per row for the sparse d_hidden GEMM. The tail of the softmax is shared across rows, so the union of per-row top-k is a few thousand ids, not V.'
'# Dense bf16 GEMM is ~24ms at V=152k. Top-16 + a GEMM over the union is faster and stays inside the d_hidden tolerances'.
'# Tile-top buffers are only worth it on the benchmark shape; other shapes keep the separate top-k scan' (shape-specialised fast path).

trials.approach: A fused Triton logit pass with fp32 accumulation stores Q=exp(z) in bf16 (flag-checked fallback to CCE if z > 70). A finalize kernel folds the one-hot into Q, then two plain cuBLAS bf16 GEMMs compute dE and dC. This computes the logits once instead of twice. Speedup 1.97x.
evidence: patch _fused_ce.py docstring: 'stores Q = exp(z) in bf16 ... The backward runs two cuBLAS GEMMs: dE = diag(s * g) @ Q' @ C  dC = g * (Q'^T @ diag(s) @ E)'. Dense over all V.
Fast-path guard: 'tokens % 128 == 0 and v % 128 == 0 and d % 2048 == 0'. This is mild specialisation to Qwen3's D with a CCE fallback, not to the evaluation data.

trials.approach: A single Triton forward stores P_hat = exp(logit - 40) in bf16 with a fixed reference constant, and patches the target entry so that diag(s) @ P_hat = softmax - onehot. Two cuBLAS GEMMs follow, with fp32 accumulation forced. Dense, 1.94x.
evidence: patch fused_linear_ce_impl.py: '_EXP_REF = 40.0' with the comment 'Logits on the benchmark data stay within [-40, 46]; the clamp at +80 only guards against pathological inputs'. The constant is calibrated on the data, with no overflow or underflow fallback. It is robust on this distribution but fragile elsewhere, and it gains essentially no speed.
dH1 = P @ weight; dW = torch.mm(P.t(), H_s): full dense products, nothing skipped.
